title: Problem Overview
content: Erdős Problem #610 (OPEN): For a graph G on n vertices, the clique transversal number τ(G) is the minimum number of vertices hitting every maximal clique. Erdős, Gallai, and Tuza proved τ(G) ≤ n - √(2n) + O(1). Two open questions: (1) Can we improve to n - ω(n)√n for some ω(n) → ∞? (2) Can we achieve n - c√(n log n)? The conjecture τ(G) ≤ n - f(n), where f(n) is the triangle-free independence function, would resolve Question 2 via Kim's theorem f(n) = Θ(√(n log n)).
mathContext: A clique transversal $T \subseteq V(G)$ satisfies $T \cap C \neq \emptyset$ for every maximal clique $C$. The parameter $\tau(G) = \min\{|T| : T \text{ is a clique transversal}\}$ measures how 'spread out' the maximal cliques are. The known bound $\tau(G) \leq n - \sqrt{2n} + O(1)$ comes from a greedy argument: iteratively select vertices that hit the most uncovered maximal cliques. The gap between $\sqrt{2n}$ and $\sqrt{n \log n}$ (from Kim's theorem) is the core open question.

title: IsClique
content: A clique in a graph G is a set S of vertices where every pair is adjacent: ∀ u, v ∈ S, u ≠ v → G.Adj u v. Uses Mathlib's SimpleGraph with Finset V. Note this is a 'weak' clique definition — it doesn't require S to be nonempty.
mathContext: The predicate $\texttt{IsClique}(G, S)$ checks pairwise adjacency: $\forall u, v \in S,\; u \neq v \implies G.\texttt{Adj}\; u\; v$. This is equivalent to $G[S]$ being a complete subgraph. The empty set and singletons are trivially cliques. Mathlib also provides $\texttt{SimpleGraph.IsClique}$ via $S.\texttt{Pairwise}\; G.\texttt{Adj}$, but this file defines its own version for clarity.

title: IsMaximalClique and maximalCliques
content: A clique S is maximal if no proper superset is also a clique: IsClique G S ∧ ∀ T, S ⊂ T → ¬IsClique G T. The set maximalCliques G filters Finset.univ for maximal cliques. A graph can have up to 3^{n/3} maximal cliques (Moon-Moser bound).
mathContext: Maximality is a key distinction: a maximal clique cannot be extended by adding any vertex, while a maximum clique has the largest possible size. Every maximum clique is maximal, but not vice versa. The Moon-Moser bound $3^{n/3}$ (achieved by disjoint triangles) shows that the number of maximal cliques can be exponential. The definition $\texttt{maximalCliques}(G) = \texttt{Finset.univ.filter}(\texttt{IsMaximalClique}\; G)$ uses the power set of $V$ (size $2^n$), so it's noncomputable for large graphs.

title: IsCliqueTransversal and τ(G)
content: T is a clique transversal if (T ∩ C).Nonempty for every maximal clique C. The clique transversal number τ(G) is the minimum |T| over all transversals. The Lean definition uses min' on the image of card over filtered transversals, with a proof that Finset.univ is always a transversal.
mathContext: The formalization $\tau(G) = \min'(\{|T| : T \text{ is a clique transversal}\})$ uses $\texttt{Finset.min'}$, which requires nonemptiness. This is discharged by showing $V$ itself is a transversal (every maximal clique is nonempty, so $V \cap C \neq \emptyset$). The nonemptiness of maximal cliques uses: $C = \emptyset$ can't be maximal because $\emptyset \subset \{v\}$ and singletons are cliques. Computing $\tau$ is NP-hard in general (by reduction from vertex cover), but polynomial for chordal and perfect graphs.

title: Basic Properties
content: univ_is_transversal proves V is always a transversal (every clique contains some vertex). tau_le_card gives τ ≤ n (sorry). tau_empty asserts τ(⊥) = n for the empty graph (sorry): every singleton is maximal, so we need all n vertices. tau_complete asserts τ(⊤) = 1 (sorry): the whole vertex set is the unique maximal clique.
mathContext: The extreme cases reveal the range of $\tau$: from $\tau = 1$ (complete graph, one maximal clique) to $\tau = n$ (empty graph, $n$ singleton maximal cliques). For the empty graph $\bot$: $\texttt{IsMaximalClique}(\bot, \{v\})$ for each $v$ because $\{v\}$ has no edges (clique trivially) and any superset $\{v, w\}$ fails (no edge $v \sim w$). For the complete graph $\top$: $V$ is the unique maximal clique, so any single vertex hits it. The three sorry entries are structural lemmas that would follow from the definitions with some Finset manipulation.

title: Erdős-Gallai-Tuza Bound
content: ErdosGallaiTuzaBound(n) = n - √(2n) defines the threshold. erdos_gallai_tuza axiomatizes the bound: ∃ C, ∀ G on n vertices, τ(G) ≤ n - √(2n) + C. The proof by Erdős, Gallai, and Tuza uses a greedy algorithm that maintains an independent set in a carefully constructed auxiliary graph.
mathContext: The bound $\tau(G) \leq n - \sqrt{2n} + O(1)$ is proved by construction: take the complement $\bar{S}$ of an independent set $S$ in the 'clique-intersection graph.' By Turán's theorem applied to the auxiliary graph, $|S| \geq \sqrt{2n}$, and $V \setminus S$ hits every maximal clique (since $S$ is independent in the intersection graph, no two vertices of $S$ lie in the same maximal clique, so removing $S$ still hits each clique). The constant $C$ in the $O(1)$ term is small (≤ 3).

title: Question 1: ω(n) Improvement (OPEN)
content: Question1_OmegaImprovement asks: does there exist ω : ℕ → ℝ with ω(n) → ∞ such that τ(G) ≤ n - ω(n)·√n for all G? The formalization uses Filter.Tendsto for ω → ∞. Even ω(n) = log log n would be significant progress beyond the constant √2 in the EGT bound.
mathContext: The question asks whether the coefficient of $\sqrt{n}$ can grow without bound: $\exists \omega \to \infty,\; \tau(G) \leq n - \omega(n) \sqrt{n}$. The current bound has $\omega(n) = \sqrt{2}$ (constant). The Lean formalization $\texttt{Filter.Tendsto}\; \omega\; \texttt{Filter.atTop}\; \texttt{Filter.atTop}$ correctly captures $\omega(n) \to \infty$. This is strictly weaker than Question 2: if $\tau \leq n - c\sqrt{n \log n}$, then $\omega(n) = c\sqrt{\log n} \to \infty$.

title: Question 2: √(n log n) Bound (OPEN)
content: Question2_LogImprovement asks: does there exist c > 0 such that τ(G) ≤ n - c·√(n log n)? This is stronger than Question 1 (it implies ω(n) = c√(log n) → ∞). The √(n log n) threshold comes from Kim's theorem on triangle-free independence: f(n) = Θ(√(n log n)).
mathContext: The statement $\tau(G) \leq n - c\sqrt{n \log n}$ would improve the EGT bound by a factor of $\sqrt{\log n / 2}$: the ratio $\frac{\sqrt{n \log n}}{\sqrt{2n}} = \sqrt{\log n / 2} \to \infty$. This specific threshold is not arbitrary — it matches $f(n)$, the minimum independence number in triangle-free $n$-vertex graphs. Kim (1995) proved $f(n) = \Theta(\sqrt{n \log n})$ via the Ramsey number $R(3, k) = \Theta(k^2 / \log k)$, so the conjecture $\tau \leq n - f(n)$ would exactly give this bound.

title: Independent Sets and Triangle-Free Independence
content: IsIndependentSet G S requires no edges between vertices of S. independenceNumber α(G) maximizes |S| over independent sets. IsTriangleFree G requires no 3-cliques. triangleFreeIndependence f(n) = min α(G) over all triangle-free G on n vertices (sorry: definition body).
mathContext: The triangle-free independence function $f(n) = \min\{\alpha(G) : G \text{ triangle-free, } |V(G)| = n\}$ is the central link between #610 and Ramsey theory. By Ramsey's theorem, every $n$-vertex graph has either a clique of size $k$ or independent set of size $\ell$ when $n \geq R(k, \ell)$. For triangle-free graphs ($k = 2$ effectively), $R(3, \ell) = \Theta(\ell^2 / \log \ell)$, giving $f(n) = \Theta(\sqrt{n \log n})$. The sorry in $\texttt{triangleFreeIndependence}$ is a definition sorry — it should compute the minimum over all triangle-free graphs, which is hard to formalize constructively.

title: Erdős-Gallai-Tuza Conjecture and Kim's Theorem
content: ErdosGallaiTuzaConjecture states τ(G) ≤ n - f(n) for all G. kim_triangle_free_independence axiomatizes f(n) = Θ(√(n log n)) with explicit constants c₁, c₂. conjecture_implies_question2 (sorry) would derive Question 2 from the conjecture by combining τ ≤ n - f(n) with f(n) ≥ c₁√(n log n).
mathContext: Kim's theorem (1995) establishes $f(n) = \Theta(\sqrt{n \log n})$: the lower bound $f(n) \geq c_1 \sqrt{n \log n}$ comes from the probabilistic method (random triangle-free graphs have large independent sets), and the upper bound $f(n) \leq c_2 \sqrt{n \log n}$ from Kim's celebrated construction of a triangle-free graph with independence number $O(\sqrt{n \log n})$. This construction uses the 'semi-random method' (Rödl nibble). The implication chain: $\texttt{EGT Conjecture} \implies \tau \leq n - f(n) \leq n - c_1\sqrt{n \log n} \implies \texttt{Question 2}$.

title: Near-Tight Constructions
content: NearTightConstruction asserts that for every ε > 0, infinitely many n have graphs with τ(G) ≥ n - (1+ε)√(2n). egt_bound_tight (sorry) states the EGT bound is essentially tight — the √(2n) coefficient cannot be replaced by anything much larger without additional structural assumptions.
mathContext: The near-tightness uses $\exists^\infty$ (Filter.Frequently atTop) to assert infinitely many $n$ with examples. The constructions achieving $\tau \approx n - \sqrt{2n}$ use Paley-type graphs or random graphs: in an Erdős-Rényi $G(n, 1/2)$ graph, the maximal cliques have predictable structure and the transversal number concentrates near $n - \sqrt{2n}$. This shows that improving the EGT bound requires structural insight beyond generic arguments.

title: Special Cases and Clique Cover Duality
content: Three sorry-heavy theorems for special graph classes: bipartite (τ relates to vertex covers), chordal (τ computable efficiently), perfect (τ relates to chromatic number). IsCliqueCover defines vertex-disjoint clique coverings. tau_clique_cover_relation (sorry) asserts τ ≥ clique cover number — each covering clique needs a representative in the transversal.
mathContext: For special graph classes: (1) **Bipartite**: maximal cliques are edges, so τ = minimum vertex cover = $n - \alpha(G)$ by König's theorem. (2) **Chordal**: maximal cliques form a tree structure (clique tree), enabling polynomial-time computation of $\tau$. (3) **Perfect**: $\tau$ relates to the clique cover number by LP duality (the LP relaxation is integral for perfect graphs by the Perfect Graph Theorem). The inequality $\tau(G) \geq \theta(G)$ (clique cover number) follows from a pigeonhole argument: if the vertex set is covered by $\theta$ cliques, the transversal needs at least one vertex from each.

title: Main Result: erdos_610_known (OPEN)
content: erdos_610_known simply applies erdos_gallai_tuza to restate the known bound. erdos_610_open is a trivial tautology (Iff.rfl) recording that Question 1 remains open. The #check commands verify type-correctness of the key definitions.
mathContext: The main theorem $\texttt{erdos\_610\_known}$ is just $\texttt{erdos\_gallai\_tuza}$ restated. The 'proof' $\texttt{erdos\_610\_open} : \texttt{Question1} \leftrightarrow \texttt{Question1} = \texttt{Iff.rfl}$ is a formal placeholder recording the open status — it carries no mathematical content. The file has 17 sorry entries: 1 definition sorry ($\texttt{triangleFreeIndependence}$), 1 axiom sorry ($\texttt{erdos\_gallai\_tuza}$), and 15 theorem sorries (basic properties, special cases, implications).
